"Stock character" is a description, not a value judgement.

Stock characters are identifiable as a certain "type." Bad writers can misuse them to avoid the hard work of characterization, but good writers can use them to create characters we instantly like or dislike, trust or mistrust. If handled correctly, stock characters can be powerful storytelling tools.

When Lucas wrote Star Wars, he populated the script with stock characters like the ones from the adventure serials he grew up watching and reading. Luke is the young, idealistic neophyte. Obi-wan is the wise, old sage. Leia is the spunky damsel in distress, and Han is the dashing rogue. These are all character types we recognize without having to be introduced to them at length.

We like Han because of his character type. Doing anything to change this aspect of his type, like fucking with his film origins, is going to weaken the strength of the character. That's not to say you can't develop him later, because the original films do that. But you can't fuck with an introduction to the audience as perfect as his introduction in ANH. (Of course, as he lost his talent, Lucas did exactly that by making Greedo shoot first.)

I think they made the decision to kill Solo off in TFA because we love his character so much. Say what you will about the movie, but that scene wouldn't have had anywhere near the emotional impact with Leia or Luke in the role. It's one of the most painful but smart decisions they made with TFA, twisting the father/son dynamic to fit Solo and Ben. The script has weaknesses, but that's not one of them.
